cands.name: Mujtaba A. Mohammed
cands.bio: Democrat and attorney who has served in the North Carolina Senate for District 38 (Mecklenburg County) since January 2019. Earlier worked as a Council for Children's Rights staff attorney and a Mecklenburg County assistant public defender. Graduate of UNC Charlotte and NC Central University School of Law.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed among his 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations. The same list includes the NC Public School Champions, Beyond The Ballot, Waves of Democracy and Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress voter guides.

In his 2018 Senate race he was endorsed by the North Carolina Association of Educators, Charlotte-Mecklenburg Association of Educators, Planned Parenthood, Black Political Caucus of Charlotte-Mecklenburg, NC AFL-CIO, NC League of Conservation Voters and The Charlotte Observer.

cands.gaps: We could not find the year Mohammed's family moved to North Carolina, only that he was raised in Charlotte. We found no statements or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, immigration enforcement or H-1B, police pay, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no documented stance on data centers or development, no foreign ties, and no controversies. The dates and length of his public defender and Council for Children's Rights work were not given in the pages we had. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys, and his 2022 survey did not address these topics.

local.label: Roots 90: He was born in Toledo, Ohio, and raised in Charlotte, where he attended Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools and later UNC Charlotte, and he is described as a longtime Charlotte resident.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State senator for District 38 since 2019; before that a staff attorney at the Council for Children's Rights and an assistant public defender in Mecklenburg County, with a J.D. from NC Central University School of Law (2013).
qual.why: Several terms of prior legislative service in the office he is running for, plus a law and public-interest career, fit the high band for writing law and the budget. No chamber leadership post is documented.
